tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

def speech_gate_envelope(ctx: Ctx, spans, total: float) -> Path | None:
    """Single mixed track (voice + game on one track): write a gain envelope that keeps the track at
    full level while you talk and pulls it down to game level between words, so digging, damage and
    splash noises stop competing with the voice. Cutaway/card spans stay at full level."""
    import wave

    import numpy as np
    if not voice_source(ctx)[3] or not ctx.S["audio"]["speech_gate"]:     # [settings] audio.speech_gate
        return None
    tr_p = ctx.proj / "work" / "transcript.json"
    g = ctx.style["audio"]["mix"].get("game_between_words_db")
    if g is None or not tr_p.exists():
        return None
    sr, pre, post, ramp = 1000, 0.12, 0.22, 0.06          # 1 kHz control rate is plenty for a gain curve
    n = int(total * sr) + 1
    floor = 10 ** (g / 20)
    env = np.full(n, floor, dtype=np.float32)
    for sp in spans:
        if sp.src_in is None:                              # meme cutaways keep their own audio untouched
            env[int(sp.out_start * sr):int(sp.out_end * sr)] = 1.0
    for seg in json.loads(tr_p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["segments"]:
        for w in seg.get("words", []):
            for sp in spans:
                a = sp.src_to_out(w["start"])
                if a is None:
                    continue
                b = sp.src_to_out(w["end"])
                b = min(b if b is not None else sp.out_end, sp.out_end)
                env[max(0, int((a - pre) * sr)):int(min(sp.out_end, b + post) * sr)] = 1.0
    k = max(1, int(ramp * sr))                             # smooth the edges (no clicks / pumping)
    env = np.convolve(env, np.ones(k) / k, mode="same").astype(np.float32)
    out = ctx.work / "speech_gate.wav"
    pcm = (np.clip(env, 0, 1) * 32767).astype(np.int16)
    with wave.open(str(out), "wb") as wf:
        wf.setnchannels(1)
        wf.setsampwidth(2)
        wf.setframerate(sr)
        wf.writeframes(pcm.tobytes())
    return out

    if g is None or not tr_p.exists():
        return None
    sr, pre, post, ramp = 1000, 0.12, 0.22, 0.06          # 1 kHz control rate is plenty for a gain curve
    n = int(total * sr) + 1
    floor = 10 ** (g / 20)
    env = np.full(n, floor, dtype=np.float32)
    for sp in spans:
        if sp.src_in is None:                              # meme cutaways keep their own audio untouched
            env[int(sp.out_start * sr):int(sp.out_end * sr)] = 1.0
    for seg in json.loads(tr_p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["segments"]:
        for w in seg.get("words", []):
            for sp in spans:
                a = sp.src_to_out(w["start"])
                if a is None:
                    continue
                b = sp.src_to_out(w["end"])
                b = min(b if b is not None else sp.out_end, sp.out_end)
                env[max(0, int((a - pre) * sr)):int(min(sp.out_end, b + post) * sr)] = 1.0
    k = max(1, int(ramp * sr))                             # smooth the edges (no clicks / pumping)
    env = np.convolve(env, np.ones(k) / k, mode="same").astype(np.float32)
    out = ctx.work / "speech_gate.wav"
    pcm = (np.clip(env, 0, 1) * 32767).astype(np.int16)
    with wave.open(str(out), "wb") as wf:
        wf.setnchannels(1)
        wf.setsampwidth(2)
        wf.setframerate(sr)
        wf.writeframes(pcm.tobytes())
    return out


def render_audio(ctx: Ctx, base: Path, overlay_audio: list[dict], spans, total: float) -> Path:
    aud = ctx.style["audio"]
    A_ = ctx.edl.get("audio", {})
    inputs: list[list] = [["-i", base]]
    chains, mix = [], []

    # dialogue bus with bleeps
    bleeps = []
    for i, b in enumerate(A_.get("bleeps", [])):
        at = resolve_time(b, spans, ctx.warnings, f"bleep[{i}]")
        if at is not None:
            bleeps.append((at, b.get("dur", 0.4)))
    mxcfg = aud["mix"]
    gate = speech_gate_envelope(ctx, spans, total)
    if gate:
        inputs.append(["-i", gate])
        chains.append(f"[{len(inputs) - 1}:a]aresample=48000,aformat=channel_layouts=stereo[gate]")
        chains.append("[0:a]aresample=48000,aformat=channel_layouts=stereo[dry]")
        dlg = "[dry][gate]amultiply," + mxcfg["voice_chain"]
    else:
        dlg = "[0:a]aresample=48000," + mxcfg["voice_chain"]
    for at, d in bleeps:
        dlg += f",volume=0:enable='between(t,{at:.3f},{at + d:.3f})'"
    music = A_.get("music", [])
    n_duck = sum(1 for m in music if m.get("duck", True))
    # sidechain keys: one per ducked music track + one for the SFX bus
    dlg += f",asplit={n_duck + 2}[dlg][sfxkey]" + "".join(f"[key{k}]" for k in range(n_duck))
    chains.append(dlg)
    mix.append("[dlg]")
    sfx_bus: list[str] = []
    for k, (at, d) in enumerate(bleeps):
        chains.append(f"sine=f={aud['bleep_hz']}:d={d:.3f}:r=48000,volume={db(aud['bleep_db'])},"
                      f"aformat=channel_layouts=stereo,adelay=delays={int(at * 1000)}:all=1[bl{k}]")
        mix.append(f"[bl{k}]")

    if o.get("asset"): ids.add(o["asset"])

    for o in e["audio"].get(k, []):
        if o.get("asset"): ids.add(o["asset"])

    x = np.frombuffer(raw, np.int16).astype(np.float32) / 32768.0

def stack_area(ctx: Ctx) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
    """(top, height) of the gameplay area as frame fractions when a short uses the stacked facecam."""
    if ctx.facecam and ctx.format == "vertical" and ctx.facecam.get("layout", "stack") == "stack":
        r = ctx.facecam.get("ratio", 0.38)
        return (r, 1 - r)
    return None


def facecam_layout(ctx: Ctx, seg: dict) -> dict | None:
    if not ctx.facecam or seg.get("facecam") is False:
        return None
    fc = ctx.facecam
    vertical = ctx.format == "vertical"
    layout = fc.get("layout") or ("stack" if vertical else "corner")
    if layout == "stack" and vertical:
        fh = int(ctx.H * fc.get("ratio", 0.38)) // 2 * 2
        return {"layout": "stack", "fw": ctx.W, "fh": fh, "gw": ctx.W, "gh": ctx.H - fh}
    fw = int(ctx.W * fc.get("size", 0.42 if vertical else 0.24)) // 2 * 2
    fh = int(fw * 9 / 16) // 2 * 2 if not fc.get("square") else fw
    return {"layout": "corner", "fw": fw, "fh": fh, "gw": ctx.W, "gh": ctx.H}


def source_segment_filter(ctx: Ctx, seg: dict, game_has_audio: bool, mic_input: bool,
                          fc_index: int | None = None) -> tuple[str, float]:
    FPS = ctx.FPS
    fcl = facecam_layout(ctx, seg) if fc_index is not None else None
    # the gameplay "area" is the whole frame, unless a stacked facecam takes the top of a short
    W, H = (fcl["gw"], fcl["gh"]) if fcl else (ctx.W, ctx.H)
    speed = seg.get("speed", 1.0)
    live = (seg["out"] - seg["in"]) / speed
    vs = ctx.sources.get("game", {}).get("video_stream", 0)
    if ctx.format == "vertical":
        # fill the tall frame: Minecraft action lives at the crosshair, so a centred crop works;
        # `frame_x` (0..1) pans the crop when the action is off-centre
        fx0 = seg.get("frame_x", 0.5)
        fit = [f"scale={W}:{H}:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase", f"crop={W}:{H}:(iw-{W})*{fx0}:(ih-{H})/2"]
    else:
        fit = [f"scale={W}:{H}:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease", f"pad={W}:{H}:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2"]
    chain = [f"setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)/{speed}", f"fps={FPS}", *fit, "setsar=1"]
    mode = ctx.mode(seg)

    # zoom + shake -> one dynamic scale + crop
    zterms, fxterms, fyterms, shake_x, shake_y = [], [], [], [], []
    for z in seg.get("zoom", []):
        a = z["at"] if "at" in z else (z["src_at"] - seg["in"]) / speed
        ri, ro = z.get("in", 0.12), z.get("out", 0.18)
        hold = z.get("hold", max(0.0, live - a - ri - ro))
        env = envelope(a, ri, hold, ro)
        zterms.append(f"{z.get('to', 1.3) - 1:.4f}*{env}")
        fx, fy = z.get("focus", [0.5, 0.5])
        fxterms.append(f"{fx - 0.5:.4f}*{env}")
        fyterms.append(f"{fy - 0.5:.4f}*{env}")
    for s in seg.get("shake", []):
        a = s["at"] if "at" in s else (s["src_at"] - seg["in"]) / speed
        amp = s.get("amp", 14) * H / 1080
        freq = s.get("freq", 18)
        env = envelope(a, 0.02, s.get("dur", 0.4), 0.1)
        zterms.append(f"{2.4 * amp / H:.5f}*{env}")
        shake_x.append(f"{amp:.2f}*sin({2 * math.pi * freq:.3f}*t)*{env}")
        shake_y.append(f"{amp * 0.8:.2f}*cos({2 * math.pi * freq * 1.3:.3f}*t)*{env}")
    if zterms:
        Z = "(1+" + "+".join(zterms) + ")"
        fx = "(0.5+" + "+".join(fxterms or ["0"]) + ")"
        fy = "(0.5+" + "+".join(fyterms or ["0"]) + ")"
        sx = "+".join(shake_x) or "0"
        sy = "+".join(shake_y) or "0"
        zw, zh = f"trunc({W}*{Z}/2)*2", f"trunc({H}*{Z}/2)*2"
        chain.append(f"scale=w='{zw}':h='{zh}':eval=frame")
        # crop's iw/ih keep the *initial* input size even when the frame grows, so derive the
        # scaled size from Z(t) directly - otherwise every zoom anchors to the top-left corner
        chain.append(f"crop={W}:{H}:x='max(0,min({zw}-{W},({zw}-{W})*{fx}+{sx}))'"
                     f":y='max(0,min({zh}-{H},({zh}-{H})*{fy}+{sy}))'")
    chain += ctx.grade_chain(seg, mode)         # [settings] look + mood grade (master switch / allowed / strength)
    if mode.get("letterbox") and ctx.format != "vertical":
        bar = int(H * 0.105)
        chain.append(f"drawbox=x=0:y=0:w=iw:h={bar}:color=black:t=fill,drawbox=x=0:y=ih-{bar}:w=iw:h={bar}:color=black:t=fill")
    for e in seg.get("effects", []):
        if e not in EFFECTS:
            ctx.warnings.append(f"segment {seg.get('id')}: unknown effect {e!r}")
            continue
        chain.append(EFFECTS[e](ctx))
    freeze = seg.get("freeze_end", 0.0)
    total = live + freeze
    tail = (f",tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop_duration={freeze:.3f}" if freeze else "") + ",format=yuv420p"
    if not fcl:
        fc = f"[0:v:{vs}]" + ",".join(chain) + tail + "[v];"
    else:
        f = ctx.facecam
        fw, fh = fcl["fw"], fcl["fh"]
        crop = f.get("crop")                                   # normalised [x, y, w, h] to frame the face
        cropf = f"crop=iw*{crop[2]}:ih*{crop[3]}:iw*{crop[0]}:ih*{crop[1]}," if crop else ""
        flip = "hflip," if f.get("flip") else ""
        cam = (f"[{fc_index}:v]setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)/{speed},fps={FPS},{cropf}{flip}"
               f"scale={fw}:{fh}:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop={fw}:{fh},format=rgba")
        fc = f"[0:v:{vs}]" + ",".join(chain) + "[g];"
        if fcl["layout"] == "stack":
            line = f.get("border", "#5FBF3A").replace("#", "0x")
            fc += cam + "[cam];"
            fc += (f"[g]pad={ctx.W}:{ctx.H}:0:{fh}:color=black[gp];[gp][cam]overlay=0:0:shortest=1,"
                   f"drawbox=x=0:y={fh - 4}:w=iw:h=8:color={line}:t=fill{tail}[v];")
        else:
            r = int(fh * 0.14)
            b = max(2, int(f.get("border_px", 6) * ctx.H / 1080))
            mask = rounded_plate(ctx, fw, fh, r, None)
            plate = rounded_plate(ctx, fw + 2 * b, fh + 2 * b, r + b, f.get("border", "#5FBF3A"))

def _norm(w: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9']", "", w.lower())


def find_phrase(words, hint, phrase, within=40.0):
    toks = [_norm(w["word"]) for w in words]
    ph = [_norm(p) for p in phrase]
    best = None
    for i in range(len(words) - len(ph) + 1):
        if abs(words[i]["start"] - hint) > within:
            continue
        if all(toks[i + k] == ph[k] for k in range(len(ph))):
            d = abs(words[i]["start"] - hint)
            if best is None or d < best[0]:
                best = (d, words[i]["start"], words[i + len(ph) - 1]["end"])
    return best[1:] if best else None



def _find_seg(segs, t):
    return next((s for s in segs if s["type"] == "source" and not s["id"].startswith("cold")
                 and s["in"] - 0.01 <= t <= s["out"] + 0.01), None)


def _split(edl, seg, t_split):
    """Split a source segment at source time t_split; events anchored beyond it follow the new tail segment."""
    segs = edl["segments"]
    k = segs.index(seg)
    tail = {kk: v for kk, v in seg.items() if kk not in ("zoom", "shake", "freeze_end")}
    tail["id"] = seg["id"] + "b"
    tail["in"] = round(t_split, 3)
    tail["out"] = seg["out"]
    if seg.get("freeze_end"):
        tail["freeze_end"] = seg["freeze_end"]
    seg["out"] = round(t_split, 3)
    seg.pop("freeze_end", None)
    for key in ("zoom", "shake"):

Rules from the creator's second review of the rd-full render (2026-10):

- Cinematic Flashback shots must have him (skin) in frame; no fullscreen aerial over fast montages (flicker). C_go_ham dropped.

# Tooling landscape & roadmap (researched Oct 2026)

**Hardware:** Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, Radeon 890M iGPU, 31 GB RAM, **no NVIDIA/CUDA**. Everything in the core runs on CPU. GPU-heavy models go through hosted APIs. ROCm on Windows supports the HX 370 only in preview and only on Python 3.12, so treat it as an optional speed-up.

## In use now

| Stage | Tool | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Orchestration | Claude Code + `/mc-edit` skill | Claude plans the edit (EDL); scripts do the mechanics |
| Composition / render | **FFmpeg 9** filtergraphs (`studio/mcstudio/render.py`) | Fast, deterministic, handles long 1080p60 timelines on CPU; AMF hardware encode available (`h264_amf`) |
| Motion graphics | **HyperFrames 0.8.x** (Apache-2.0, HTML→video, skills installed) | Bespoke title cards, counters, maps; renders `--format mov` with alpha that the ffmpeg pass composites |
| Transcription | **faster-whisper** large-v3-turbo, int8 CPU | Word timestamps for captions and cut planning. Pinned to Python 3.12 because CTranslate2 has no Windows 3.14 wheels |
| Captions / text | libass (ASS) burned in by ffmpeg | Karaoke highlight, pop/shake/slide anims, channel fonts from the pack |
| Signals | numpy loudness envelopes + ffmpeg scene score | Yells, game booms, scene changes, dead air |
| Asset DB | SQLite + FTS5 (`studio/catalog/assets.db`) | 1,455 assets, LLM-tagged with moment taxonomy, ratings, copyright risk, hit timing, key colour |
| Mix / loudness | Voice-relative gain staging per role (catalog `loud_db`), SFX bus ducked under voice, speech gate for single-track recordings, static gain → −14 LUFS + −1.5 dBFS limiter | SFX never bury the voice; YouTube target without hidden compression |
| Ducking | ffmpeg `sidechaincompress` keyed by dialogue | Music sits under the voice automatically |

## Added since the first version
- 9:16 Shorts generator, mood modes, colour looks, auto engagement zooms, facecam layouts, narrator avatar, motion
  library (HyperFrames), Stock Library, one-click `mcs make`, render-time cut guard, voice-relative mixing,
  unified 6k-asset pack with exact + perceptual de-duplication (`catalog/dedupe.py`) and content-stable ids.

## Next upgrades (in priority order)

0. **Voice/game separation for single-track recordings.** Run Demucs (htdemucs, CPU, about real-time) or `audio-separator` (MDX/Roformer ONNX) to split a mixed OBS track into voice and game stems. This gives clean captions, independent game volume, and no game noise under the voice. The speech gate (`game_between_words_db`) is the stop-gap. The real fix is recording the mic on its own OBS track.
1. **Gemini video understanding** (agentic video mode, Gemini 3.x Flash, Sep 2026): send the gameplay and get timestamped moment labels (deaths, mobs, loot, builds). This feeds the beat sheet alongside the transcript. Needs a `GEMINI_API_KEY`. It would be a new `mcs vision <slug>` stage writing `work/vision.json`.
2. **Semantic asset search:** LAION-CLAP embeddings for audio and SigLIP 2 for video/image keyframes, stored with sqlite-vec next to `assets.db`. This enables "find a sound like a cartoon slip" beyond the tags. Indexing runs on CPU.
3. **Laughter/scream detection** on the mic with PANNs CNN14 (AudioSet), CPU. It's more precise than loudness peaks for finding funny moments.
4. **Filler-word removal** ("um", "uh") from word timestamps. The scaffold already has the data.
5. **Noise reduction** on the mic: ffmpeg `arnndn` (RNNoise, built in) or DeepFilterNet3. Add it as a per-project option.
6. **WebM-alpha conversion** (13 Minecraft transitions): 12 Minecraft item transitions are VP8-alpha WebMs this ffmpeg build can't decode. Convert them once through HyperFrames/Chrome to ProRes 4444 (they are hidden from the finder until then).
7. **Thumbnails:** a HyperFrames still composition (face cutout + item + Lemon Milk / Luckiest Guy text) with the pack's thumbnail lines and borders. The background can come from a hosted image model.
8. **Generative fill-ins (APIs):** ElevenLabs SFX v2 for missing sounds, Lyria / ACE-Step for custom beds, Gemini TTS for narrator gags.

## Evaluated, not adopted (yet)

- **Remotion 4.x:** strong, but it's React and needs a license for teams of 4+. HyperFrames covers the same ground and is already installed.
- **video-use** (browser-use, MIT): a Claude Code skill with the same idea (transcript → LLM EDL → ffmpeg). It's a good reference, but it depends on ElevenLabs Scribe and targets talking-head edits. Our pipeline is gameplay- and meme-specific.
- **auto-editor:** our scaffold does word-aware dead-air cutting, so its audio-threshold cutting is redundant.
- **NLE MCP servers** (DaVinci Resolve, Premiere, CapCut): less deterministic than calling ffmpeg directly. Revisit if you want to hand off to a human editor (export EDL → Resolve timeline).
- **Local video generation** (Wan, LTX-2): needs NVIDIA VRAM; use hosted models if ever needed.

# Token cost plan: first video ~1.5M tokens -> target well under 300k

Where the tokens went on rd-full (from how the session actually ran; not a measured per-call ledger):

| Sink | Why it was expensive | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Iterating on the cut by hand | ~10 review/feedback rounds, each re-reading edit.json, builder output and logs | Encode every past correction as a rule in code (done partly: learning/prefs, memory). Rules in `style.json`/pacing gates mean the first render is already close |
| Looking at frames / contact sheets | Every image read is large | One automated QA report (text) per render: static scan, music-gap scan, meme length, zoom-framing check, last-frame check. Only open an image when the text report flags something |
| Reading big files into context | edit.json (224 segs), transcripts, builder scripts re-read repeatedly | Write small summary files (timeline.md: id, real start, length, kind). Query with scripts, never cat big JSON |
| Full re-renders to test a hunch | Each render ~25 min plus log polling and follow-up reads | Render only changed segments (cache already exists), preview at 480p, trust text QA first |
| Long polling / status chatter | Waiting loops, repeated tails | Use background tasks + one completion notification; no polling |
| Tagging and cataloguing with agents | Thousands of assets, image strips | Already done once; new assets only (incremental). Use a cheaper model (Haiku/Sonnet) for tagging, Opus only for story decisions |
| Rework from drift bugs | Music timing drift, cache keys, silent-meme gain | Fixed at the root this round; add regression checks to `mcs check` |

## Concrete plan, in order of payoff

1. **Auto-QA gate (`mcs verify rd-full`)**: runs after every render and prints a ~30-line text report: static/buzz scan, music coverage per scene (no gaps, level vs voice), meme and freeze durations, zoom framing, first 10 s / last frame facts, word-clip count, duration. Replaces most screenshot review. Scripts already exist (`projects/rd-full/aq.py`, `static_scan.py`, `tl.py`); promote into `mcstudio`.
2. **Keep a per-project timeline summary** (`work/timeline.md`) regenerated on build, with real render times. Feedback like "at 8:56" maps to a segment with one grep.
3. **Promote the story builder into a reusable template**: `build_v3.py` and `rd_manual3.py` are video-specific. A new video should be: transcript -> windows proposal (cheap model) -> one human-feedback round, not a rewrite.
4. **Model tiering**: Sonnet for research, tagging, mechanical edits and QA triage; the strongest model only for story selection and resolving contradictions in feedback. Haiku for catalog tagging.
5. **Preview-first loop**: 480p/30 fps preview render of just the scenes under review; full 1080p60 only at the end.
6. **Deterministic pre-processing before any LLM sees footage**: audio events (PANNs/laughter), scene cuts, OCR flags, voice envelope, all cached per recording, so the model reads a 2-page beat sheet instead of raw transcripts.
7. **Do not re-tag or re-read the asset library**: prompt the finder through `mcs assets find`, which is already SQL, never list folders.
8. **Memory/skills as the cache**: every review comment becomes a rule file once (`learning/notes.md` -> `prefs.json` -> code). Next video starts with the creator's taste already enforced.

## Expectation
Realistic: video 2 at 400-600k (rules exist, builder reusable), video 3+ under 300k, mostly one story pass, one feedback round and verification by text.

content.text:
Three Sonnet researchers have finished, and I wrote the token-cost plan myself. All four reports are in `studio/docs/research/`. I haven't implemented any of it yet.

**Reports**
- [style_and_skills.md](studio/docs/research/style_and_skills.md): your WeAreNoCode folder plus YouTube editing-style research.
- [automation_tools.md](studio/docs/research/automation_tools.md): ranked tool adoption table.
- [effects_and_motion.md](studio/docs/research/effects_and_motion.md): 17 effect and transition recipes.
- [token_cost_plan.md](studio/docs/research/token_cost_plan.md): how to bring the cost down.

**Your folder**
- The WeAreNoCode skill is built for talking-head and tutorial videos, so its style rules don't fit Minecraft.
- Its quality-check ideas do fit: a cut-edge audit, a gap scan, and teardown measurement of reference videos. These are worth adding.
- The `.crdownload` file is just a duplicate of the finished zip, so it can be deleted.

**Tools to add**
- **Adopt now:**
  - PANNs for laughter and scream detection.
  - ffmpeg's RNNoise for mic noise reduction.
  - Gemini video understanding on small proxy copies, to label gameplay moments (needs an API key).
  - PySceneDetect plus SigLIP2 for semantic asset search.
  - Voice/game separation, only for single-track recordings.
- **Later:** DeepFilterNet3, Vulkan whisper.cpp, and generative audio models, which are slow on CPU.
- **Skip:** ffmpeg MCP servers, clip-farm clones and local video generation. Nothing beats our current skill plus the deterministic ffmpeg edit list.

**Effects**
- This ffmpeg has no gl-transitions filter, so custom xfade expressions are the way to build block-wipe, pixelize, whip, glitch, speed-ramp and damage-flash transitions.
- 13 of the 17 recipes were tested on small clips. Item pop, XP orb and achievement toast need pre-rendered HyperFrames alpha clips.
- Kenney and Freesound CC0 are safe asset sources. Pixabay is not CC0.

**Style**
- Only one hard number came out of the web research: MrBeast went from 38 to 23 cuts per minute from 2023 to 2024, with longer, calmer shots.
- There is no Minecraft-specific data, so we'd need 3–5 reference videos from you to measure real pacing. That means downloading them, which I won't do without your OK.

**Token cost** (the plan's per-video targets are my own estimates, not measured)
- The biggest sinks were repeated feedback rounds, image reviews, re-reading large files, full re-renders to test hunches, and bugs that were fixed in code after the fact.
- The main fix is an automatic text quality report after every render, covering static, music gaps, meme length, zoom framing and the last frame, so I rarely need to look at frames.
- Other fixes: a small timeline summary file so "at 8:56" resolves in one lookup, a reusable story builder instead of a per-video rewrite, a cheaper model for tagging and mechanical work, and 480p previews.
- Realistic target: about 400–600k tokens for video 2 and under 300k from video 3 on.

Two things need your decision before I build:
1. **Gemini key.** Do you want the Gemini moment detection? It's the biggest quality jump but needs an API key and has a small cost per video.
2. **Reference videos.** Are you OK with me downloading 3–5 reference Minecraft videos you pick, so I can measure real pacing?

Without answers I'd start with the free, local items: the automatic quality report, noise reduction, laughter detection, and the effect recipes.

"""Measure pacing of a finished video: cuts/min (scene score), shot-length stats, first-30s density, loudness, silence share.
usage: uv run python learning/teardown.py video.mp4 [more.mp4 ...]   -> prints a table, writes learning/teardown.json"""
import json, re, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np

def dur(p):
    return float(subprocess.run(["ffprobe","-v","error","-show_entries","format=duration","-of","csv=p=0",str(p)],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout)

def cuts(p, thr=0.28):
    r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg","-v","info","-i",str(p),"-vf",f"scale=320:-2,select='gt(scene,{thr})',showinfo","-an","-f","null","-"],
                       capture_output=True,text=True,encoding="utf-8",errors="replace")
    return [float(m) for m in re.findall(r"pts_time:([0-9.]+)", r.stderr)]

def audio(p):
    r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg","-v","error","-i",str(p),"-vn","-ac","1","-ar","16000","-f","s16le","-"],capture_output=True)
    x = np.frombuffer(r.stdout, dtype=np.int16).astype(np.float32)/32768
    n = 1600
    env = 20*np.log10(np.array([np.sqrt((x[i:i+n]**2).mean()) for i in range(0,len(x)-n+1,n)])+1e-7)
    return env

def stats(p):
    d = dur(p); c = cuts(p); env = audio(p)
    shots = np.diff([0]+c+[d])
    first30 = sum(1 for t in c if t < 30)
    per_min = len(c)/(d/60)
    # share of 10 s windows with no cut at all (dead stretches) and loud-peak rate
    wins = [sum(1 for t in c if a <= t < a+10) for a in np.arange(0, d-10, 10)]
    quiet = (env < -50).mean()
    peaks = (env > np.percentile(env, 50)+14).mean()
    return {"file": Path(p).name, "min": round(d/60,1), "cuts_per_min": round(per_min,1), "median_shot_s": round(float(np.median(shots)),1),
            "p90_shot_s": round(float(np.percentile(shots,90)),1), "first30s_cuts": first30,
            "windows10s_without_cut_pct": round(100*sum(1 for w in wins if w==0)/max(1,len(wins))),
            "silence_pct": round(100*quiet,1), "loud_burst_pct": round(100*peaks,1), "p50_db": round(float(np.percentile(env,50)),1),
            "p95_db": round(float(np.percentile(env,95)),1)}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    out = [stats(p) for p in sys.argv[1:]]
    for o in out: print(o, flush=True)
    Path(__file__).with_name("teardown.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=1))
EOF

I downloaded your 5 reference videos at 480p and measured their pacing against our render. We are much slower than all of them.

| | Cuts per minute | Longest typical shot | 10 s stretches with no cut |
|---|---|---|---|
| The 5 reference videos | 9.8–18.7 | 6.6–16.8 s | 10–35% |
| Our video | 7.1 | 22.1 s | 46% |

- **Cuts and uncut stretches:** four of the five references cut 15–19 times a minute. Ours cuts 7.1 times a minute, and almost half our 10-second stretches have no cut at all.
- **Shot length:** typical shots in the references are about 2 s, and ours are 3.1 s.
- **Loudness:** the references sit around −17 to −20 dB median loudness, and ours is quieter at −24 dB.
- **Caveat:** this only counts hard cuts, not zooms or overlays, so treat it as a style target.

**What this means for the next edit**
- **Targets:** at least 15 hard cuts a minute, no shot longer than about 9 s, at most 15% cut-less stretches, and 10 or more cuts in the first 30 s.
- **How to hit them:** long talking stretches need cutaways, punch-ins or pickup cuts so something changes every few seconds.

I saved the numbers in `studio/docs/research/reference_teardown.md` and added them to memory.

The five videos total about 600 MB in `studio/learning/reference_videos/`. They are only used to measure pacing and can be deleted once you're happy with the numbers.

Next, say if you want me to build these into the pipeline:
- a text quality report after every render covering static, music gaps, pacing and the end frame
- a pacing check that adds cuts automatically
- noise reduction and laughter detection

Four more Sonnet researchers are working: After Effects-grade motion graphics, cinematic Flashback shots, sound design and asset placement, and pro-editor knowledge and training.

**Gemini cost.** I can't confirm Gemini's current prices. The research flagged that as unverified. It is a paid API with some free-tier allowance, and no key is set up here yet. I'd expect cents to low single-digit dollars per 20-minute video if we send small 480p copies, but check Google's pricing page before relying on that. I won't enable it without your key and your go-ahead.

**Flashback shots.** I agree they're weak. They are generic wide aerials with a tiny player, flat vanilla lighting and drifting orbits that don't relate to the action. The biggest gap is that the game has no shaders installed, so everything renders flat. The cinematic-shots researcher will cover close hero-angle recipes, shaders (checking whether they run on your AMD iGPU), and automatic rejection of bad shots. I'll report when the four reports are in, before touching Minecraft.

**Quality report.** `mcs verify` is built and runs on the current render. It flagged the real pacing problems (7.1 cuts/min against a 15 target, 46% cut-less stretches). Its static check gave false alarms at the first sensitivity, so I raised the audio sample rate and I'm re-running it now.

**Voice cut-offs and skipped context.** I measured both on the last render rather than guessing, since the render's own guard was extending cuts by at most 0.35 s.
- **Cuts over your voice:** 18 clips ended while you were still talking, and 42 clips began mid-phrase.
- **Skipped context:** 27 jumps skipped 6 or more words of context, some 40–86 words, and several of the next clips opened on "it", "that" or "so".
- **Fixes:**
  - Clips now run to the end of the phrase (at the next breath between words, or the end of the silence).
  - Clips back up to the phrase start instead of opening mid-word.
  - Tiny gaps inside continuous speech are closed so no word is chopped.
  - Jumps that open on a pronoun or skip lots of speech get a lead-in phrase of up to 3.5 s.
  - Events keep their timing when a clip's start moves.
- **Result on the new edit list:** 18 cuts over your voice became 4, and 42 mid-phrase starts became 6.
- **Skipped context is only partly fixed.** Only 3 jumps got a lead-in. Most big skips are whole scenes that I deliberately jumped between, and I can't reliably tell which ones you'd feel as missing context. If a specific jump still feels wrong after you watch it, give me the timestamp and I'll fix that one.
- **Length:** the render comes out at 24.5 min after the fixes.

**Research** (all in `studio/docs/research/`, with the cost plan and effects recipes from before)
- `cinematic_shots.md`: why the replay shots look bad and the upgrade stack.
  - **Cause:** the camera sits so high and far that the player is about 2–3% of the frame, shots are chosen by transcript position instead of story beat, and there's no grade, bloom or speed ramp.
  - **Fix order:** close hero framing matched to the story beat, forced golden-hour lighting, a post grade/bloom/vignette/grain chain, speed ramps, a resource pack, and Iris shaders last.
  - **Verified:** Iris and Complementary shaders list MC 1.21.11. Whether your Radeon iGPU runs them is untested.
- `ae_grade_motion.md`: how to get After Effects-style effects.
  - **Hit effects and tracking:** ffmpeg shake, punch, whip and speed-ramp presets, then tracked callouts and text that passes behind the player.
  - **3D and parallax:** three.js 3D titles and blocks inside HyperFrames, then depth-map parallax on stills.
  - **Blender:** last priority, since three.js covers most 3D.
  - **Caveat:** this report was written from knowledge, not live web research, and is mostly untested.
- `sound_and_placement.md`: numeric rules for layered impacts, SFX 0 to −40 ms ahead of the visual, ducking values, and beat-snapping cuts.
  - **Sources:** Freesound CC0, Sonniss and Kenney are safe. Avoid Stable Audio Open (non-commercial licence).
  - **Not verified:** the ElevenLabs SFX price and the Sonniss 2026 licence text still need checking.
- `pro_editor_knowledge.md`: story and edit grammar rules, a scoring rubric, and a plan to train the editor from reference videos.

**Decisions**
- I'll leave Gemini out entirely and use only local tools.
- I'll hold off on the Flashback shots until you've watched this render and the new editor rules are in. Redoing them means closing Minecraft and OBS again and a long export.

I'll report the new verify result and cut check once the render finishes.
